summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of chronic leg ulcers, diastolic heart failure, aortic valve replacement, and obesity was admitted for worsening left lower extremity pain, erythema, and copious yellow-green drainage following completion of oral cephalexin. She reported shaking chills and inadequate pain control with home morphine. Evaluation revealed cellulitis without evidence of osteomyelitis on X-ray. She was treated with IV antibiotics, and wound culture grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa, sensitive to the chosen regimen. A minor wound debridement was performed, and her infection, pain, and swelling improved. Her acute kidney injury resolved, INR normalized on warfarin, and heart failure remained stable. She was transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin, discharged home with home health wound care, and scheduled for follow-up with infectious disease, wound care, and lymphedema services.
